validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, independently documented project, not a GEM-only entity. Pipeline & Gas Journal (2018-02-21) reports Tellurian subsidiary Haynesville Global Access Pipeline LLC launched a non-binding open season for a proposed 42-inch, ~200-mile, $1.4B, 2 Bcf/d pipeline from the Haynesville/Bossier shale region (Claiborne Parish) to interconnects near Gillis, Calcasieu Parish, LA. Corroborated by Tellurian's own January 2020 investor presentation (same figures), the EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' workbook (operator 'Haynesville Global Access Pipeline LLC (Tellurian Inc.)', LA, 2000 MMcf/d), NGI (2020-08-13, Jamison Cocklin) and S&P Global Platts (2020-08-12, Harry Weber), both reporting Tellurian deferring the project. Not GEM-only. CLASSIFICATION: transmission is correct -- a 42in/160-200mi/2 Bcf/d interstate-scale line is far above gathering/lateral scale; oilandgas360's open-season article (currently cited) covers a long-haul shipper open season consistent with transmission. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 44-row roster, especially the Haynesville egress corridor (P5115 LEG, P6843 LEAP, P2523 Delhi Connector, P7807/P7808 Gillis-area, P7831 Pelican, P7832 NGPL, P2737 Delta Express, P2559 Magnolia) -- none shares P0285's sponsor (Tellurian), route (Haynesville/Claiborne Parish to Gillis/Calcasieu Parish), or specs (42in/2000 MMcf/d/$1.4B). P2523 Delhi Connector is a distinct, separate Tellurian project (Delhi, LA to Gillis, LA, 180mi per the same EIA workbook entry) explicitly named alongside HGAP in the same 2019 open-season announcement and 2020 deferral coverage -- sibling projects, not duplicates of each other. No relabel/double-count found. CANCELLATION TIMING: see status_reviews -- CancelledYear=2024 is best read as GEM's own dormancy inference (ShelvedYear 2020 + 4y), not a sourced discrete cancellation event; recommend ShelvedCancelledType='inferred'.

Diameter (42in), Capacity (2000 MMcf/d / 2.0 Bcf/d) and SegmentCost ($1.4B) all agree across every source checked -- only Length disagrees, and the 200-mile figure is the better-corroborated one (three independent-origin documents spanning 2018-2020 vs. one company-site origin for 160mi). Recommend correcting LengthKnown to 200; leaving the 160mi figure as recorded would misstate a value that is actually only single-origin-sourced.
